sources.title: MASSIVE-Agents: A Benchmark for Multilingual Function-Calling in 52 Languages
sources.supports: Broad multilingual function-calling coverage and evidence of large cross-language performance variation.
sources.does_not_establish: That performance gaps are caused specifically by semantic action selection rather than translation, interface, data, or evaluator contracts.

inspection_spans.observation: The benchmark transforms parallel multilingual utterances into function-calling tasks across 52 languages and reports low average AST accuracy with severe low-resource failures.
inspection_spans.does_not_establish: That performance gaps are caused specifically by semantic action selection rather than translation, interface, data, or evaluator contracts.

inspection_spans.observation: Results depend on language, model, prompting template, translated descriptions, filtering, and AST/function-selection metrics.
inspection_spans.does_not_establish: That performance gaps are caused specifically by semantic action selection rather than translation, interface, data, or evaluator contracts.

sources.title: Lost in Execution: On the Multilingual Robustness of Tool Calling in Large Language Models
sources.supports: A controlled distinction between semantic tool selection and language-interface execution failure.
sources.does_not_establish: Long-horizon behavior, all languages, real deployment incidence, or the superiority of one interface design.

inspection_spans.observation: Correct intent and tool selection can still yield non-executable calls when parameter values use the user's language rather than the interface convention.
inspection_spans.does_not_establish: Long-horizon behavior, all languages, real deployment incidence, or the superiority of one interface design.

inspection_spans.observation: Execution-interface violations dominate for some languages; translation mitigations help but introduce semantic drift and do not recover English performance.
inspection_spans.does_not_establish: Long-horizon behavior, all languages, real deployment incidence, or the superiority of one interface design.

inspection_spans.observation: The study is single-turn, uses three languages and an English-parameter interface, and treats mitigations as diagnostic probes.
inspection_spans.does_not_establish: Long-horizon behavior, all languages, real deployment incidence, or the superiority of one interface design.
